title: Efficient Quantum Optimization via Dissipative False Vacuum Decay
authors: Zhi-Hao Huang, Tian-Mu Hu, Shuaifan Cao, Ye Lu, Xiaopeng Li
abstract: Efficient quantum solvers for computationally hard problems are highly desirable for near-term quantum platforms. Here, we propose a cavity-based dissipative quantum solver for a class of NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems encoded in atomic-spin Hamiltonians with a few discrete single-spin-flip transition energies. We show that the cavity-based quantum solver exploits dissipative false-vacuum decay in configuration space to facilitate escape from metastable local minima in rugged energy landscapes. Numerical studies of MaxCut and Maximum Independent Set identify favorable parameter regions for ground-state preparation. Based on the finite-size scalings of the median mixing time and instance-averaged ground-state preparation probability, we estimate time complexities for our solver that are more favorable than those of standard Grover search. These results highlight cavity dissipation as a controllable resource for quantum optimization.
summary: This paper proposes using a cavity-based quantum solver that leverages dissipative false-vacuum decay to solve NP-hard optimization problems like MaxCut and MIS. By coupling the spin system to a lossy cavity, the dissipation acts as a controlled resource, guiding the system efficiently out of local energy minima toward the true ground state. The resulting time complexity estimates are shown to surpass those of standard quantum search methods.
main_problem: Developing efficient quantum solvers for computationally hard, NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems.
main_result: The authors show that cavity dissipation can be harnessed as a controllable resource to drive the system out of local minima toward the ground state, achieving time complexities better than standard Grover search.
method: The mechanism relies on exploiting dissipative false-vacuum decay by coupling the spin system to a lossy optical cavity, which facilitates irreversible population transfer.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a cavity-based quantum solver described by a Lindblad master equation involving a problem Hamiltonian (Ising-type), a coupling Hamiltonian, and a photon Hamiltonian. The dynamics are governed by the interplay between coherent tunneling and photon loss.
key_observables: Ground-State Preparation Probability ($P_g(T)$) and median mixing time ($t_{mix}$).
important_parameters: Photon leakage rate ($\kappa$), cavity detuning ($\Delta$), and atom-photon coupling strength ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the interplay between coherent transitions and irreversible photon-loss-induced relaxation, and the time complexity estimate excludes state preparation and readout costs.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical realization and the energy-shell picture of dissipative dynamics, showing how photon loss drives population flow toward the ground state. Other figures show $P_g(T)$ and $t_{mix}$ scaling for MaxCut and MIS.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the Hamiltonian and the dissipative mechanism (dissipative false-vacuum decay), presents numerical results for MaxCut and MIS, and concludes by estimating favorable time complexities compared to existing quantum search algorithms.
why_interesting: This work directly applies concepts from open quantum systems and cavity QED (dissipation, cavity coupling) to solve a fundamental problem in quantum computation (optimization), making it highly relevant to AMO physicists studying engineered quantum dynamics.
